title: Why You Jolt When Someone Touches You From Behind
hook: Feeling a sudden jolt when someone touches you unexpectedly?

narration.text: That's your ancient survival reflex kicking in, designed to keep you safe.
Your brain interprets an unexpected touch from behind as a potential threat.
It instantly triggers a fight or flight response, even if there's no real danger.
This causes your muscles to tense and your heart rate to spike in an instant.
It is a primal alert system, helping you react quickly to the unknown.
This explains why you jump, even when it is just a friend.
Like this if it surprised you and subscribe for more insights into your amazing body.

description: Ever wondered why you flinch so hard when someone touches your shoulder unexpectedly? It's not just you being jumpy, it's a deep-seated survival mechanism at play. Learn how your brain's ancient threat detection system works.
topic: Why you feel a jolt if someone touches you unexpectedly from behind. This is a survival reflex.
